name: Session timers
summary: See when a session will wake itself next: a clock chip beside the session shows the time to its next live timer, and opens a read-only list of every timer it set.
description: Claude Code records the scheduling a session does for itself as tool calls in its own transcript: a self wakeup (the /loop mechanism) and session-only cron jobs, which a later call can cancel. The attention watcher reads them from the session's current conversation once per cycle and counts a timer as live only while the claude process that set it is alive and started before it, because these timers live inside that process and die with it. The session listing carries the live count and the soonest fire time; a codex or shell session is not applicable, never zero. A clock chip beside the subagent chip shows the time to the next fire (18m, 3h, due) or the live count, in the agents drawer (cozy and detailed density) and the running sessions cell. Since issue #945's follow-up (#1039), when a SUB-AGENT is what parked on its own open shell or Monitor - the case that used to show a session as working_subagent with nothing on screen explaining why - the list also names each one: which sub-agent, its task, its kind and how long it has been open, in one already-redacted sentence with no command or output ever shown. The same sentence appears in the status light's tooltip when that is the reason the light reads working_subagent. Nothing here feeds the light's colour or the auto-sleep idle clock.
where: Agents drawer, every density: a small icon-only clock marker beside a session row's status light, drawn while that session has a live timer - hover it for the count and next-fire time.
Agents drawer, cozy or detailed density: a small clock chip beside a session row, drawn only while that session has a live timer.
Home screen, running sessions cell: the same chip beside the session's status light.
how_to: Have a claude session schedule itself, for example with /loop or by asking it to check back later, or to run something every 15 minutes.
Watch the icon-only marker and, at cozy/detailed, the clock chip appear beside that session within one watcher cycle.
Hover the marker, or read the chip, for the time to its next fire.
Click the chip to open the read-only list of every timer the conversation set, live ones first.
Restart the session: its timers were held by the old process, so the marker and chip go away and the list marks them lost.
examples: A session polling a CI run every 15 minutes shows a chip reading 12m, so you know when it will next report without opening it.
After a reboot the chip is gone and the list says lost, which tells you the loop needs starting again.
media_exempt: screenshots and captures are not part of the open source export
